dimension_justifications.soundness: Individual measurements are unusually carefully scoped, and the per-component Store accounting in Appendix C (p.17, Table 4) is exactly checkable against the paper's own format identity. But the central object of the paper was never executed as specified: Section 4.3 (p.5) states that the implementation behind Tables 1-2 'materializes a full private copy of the dequantized entry per query, so it shares nothing and exercises neither borrowing nor copy-on-write,' while Section 4.4 (p.5), Section 5.1 'Executed systems' (p.6) and Section 5.5 (p.8) state that every FORKAUDIT verdict and the allocator study run on full-prefix BF16 KV with no split depth and no quantization. The composite protocol drawn in Figure 1 therefore has no end-to-end execution behind it, and the paper's ownership discipline transfers to its own headline configuration 'by design argument only' (Section 5.6, p.9). Separately, the comparison that carries the strongest abstract claim -- 'full-prefix Q8 ... at -3.78 points' -- rests on a self-implemented uniform-Q8 arm whose degradation is inconsistent with the KV-quantization literature the paper itself cites and tabulates (Table 19, p.28, records KVTuner as 'nearly lossless 3.25-bit'); the paper never investigates that discrepancy. These are substantive gaps that materially reduce confidence in the comparative conclusions, though not in the raw byte accounting.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is precise but not readable at the level a reviewer needs to extract a claim. The abstract (p.1) is a single unbroken block of nested numbers and qualifications in which the actual contribution is hard to locate; three separate reference values for the same object (136.235, 140.34, 106.235 MiB/doc) appear across Tables 1 (p.7), 2 (p.8) and Appendix C (p.17) and require a five-line footnote to reconcile. Thirty appendix tables are dominated by internal audit bookkeeping (Tables 5-13, 24-30) whose relevance to any manuscript claim is not signposted, while Figure 3 (p.18) is captioned by the authors as 'not experimental evidence.' The main text respects the 9-page limit, the reproducibility and ethics statements are present, and the limitations section (5.6, p.9) is admirably explicit; but organization and hedging density materially obstruct evaluation.
dimension_justifications.contribution: After the paper's own disclaimers, very little claimed novelty remains. The split-replay primitive is the authors' prior CoMem (Liu et al., 2026a;b), explicitly 'not claim[ed] as new' (Section 2, p.2-3, and Table 14, p.26). The group-wise asymmetric quantizer is disclaimed as prior art (Section 2, p.3: 'Q-COMEM claims none of its mechanisms'). Per-layer width assignment is disclaimed as 'an application of an established design surface, not a new selection method' (p.3). FORKAUDIT's detection increment is reduced by the authors to 'transition-time localization, not exclusive detection' (Section 5.5, p.8), on a configuration that is not the proposed method. What is left is (a) the observation that a hybrid split-replay entry must also retain lower KV/conv/recurrent state, and (b) the measurement of what an off-the-shelf quantizer does to that entry. (a) is a real but narrow architectural observation already central to Marconi and HYPIC; (b) reproduces the format arithmetic exactly (Appendix C, p.17: 180/180 rows satisfy the ceiling identity, and no reported ratio exceeds it). The result is a bounded, honest, incremental measurement study rather than new capability, and its capacity win is bought at worse TTFT than both endpoints (Section 5.3, p.7).

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends the authors' prior CoMem split-replay scheme to hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLMs under a capacity-first objective. An offline Write runs a document to split depth j and group-quantizes the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and the convolution/recurrent state a later query needs; an online Read dequantizes that entry, is intended to share only immutable document tensors while keeping mutable request state private, and replays the query through the lower layers before reconstructing the upper suffix. A separate fail-closed trace protocol, FORKAUDIT, defines seven ownership targets (identity, prefix immutability, private ownership, tail COW, host-side call provenance, cross-arm equivalence, cross-N consistency) with explicit coverage semantics. Empirically, on 60 archived Qasper/2WikiMQA items with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e, a frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy at j=7 reduces mean retained tensor payload from 136.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (14.10x; 10.9965x against an all-BF16 reference) at a paired mean-F1 difference of -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] against the full-prefix arm. Timing is adverse on every axis (TTFT 0.656 s vs 0.181 s full-prefix and 0.636 s dense; throughput 7.15-7.19 vs 13.38 tok/s; TPOT within 2.5%). A third system reports that shared-document KV lowers the post-priming allocator delta 54.5% final / 42.2% peak at N=32 against a full-copy control. The paper explicitly declines claims about total process memory, Recall, edge performance, and broad quality preservation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The per-component retained-state accounting for a hybrid split-replay entry (Section 4.1, Eq. 2, p.4; Appendix C, Table 4, p.17). The paper establishes, with a checkable identity that all 180 item-policy pairs satisfy exactly, that counting only the depth-j residual understates the state a hybrid deployment must retain, that 30.000 of the 136.235 MiB/document full-prefix reference is FP32 GDN excess rather than a packing gain, and that the like-for-like all-BF16 ratio is 10.9965x with a 2.97x quantization step. This dtype-versus-packing decomposition is a genuine and unusually honest measurement contribution that most KV-compression papers do not supply.
strengths: Unusually disciplined denominator hygiene. Store is defined as an entry-owned physical byte-range union and kept explicitly separate from allocator deltas, process/NVML memory, workspace, and admitted capacity (Section 5.1 p.6, Section 5.6 p.9); the paper states which of the three cohorts supports which claim and refuses to pool them.

The paper self-corrects the most flattering reading of its own headline: it discloses that 30.000 MiB/document of the 136.235 MiB reference is FP32 dtype excess, prints the all-BF16 restatement (10.9965x), and shows in Appendix C (p.17) why the printed 3.590x split-to-frozen step would otherwise appear to violate the Q4 format ceiling.

Prior art is disclaimed rather than repackaged. Section 2 (p.3) states outright that the quantizer is the standard asymmetric affine form used by FlexGen and that per-layer bit assignment is prior art from KVTuner/AsymKV; Table 14 (p.26) states that CoMem 'supplies the split-replay foundation; we do not claim that primitive as new.' This is the correct posture and is rare.
Blank cells for unmeasured metrics. Recall is never imputed; the paper repeatedly states 'blank cells are unmeasured metrics, not zeros' (Table 1 footnote, p.7).

The negative results are reported at the same prominence as the positive ones: adverse TTFT against both endpoints (Section 5.3, p.7), the aggressive policy's interval below zero (Table 1), and the fork's 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB generation-increment penalty against the paged-prefix baseline (Table 18, p.27).
questions: Why does full-prefix Q8 lose 3.78 F1 points? Group-64 asymmetric 8-bit KV quantization is reported as essentially lossless throughout the literature you cite, and your own Table 19 (p.28) records KVTuner as 'nearly lossless' at 3.25 bits. Is the 3.78-point loss a property of Qwen3.5's GDN state under this codec, or an artifact of the arm's implementation? Please diagnose it before using it as the comparator for the abstract's '3.41-point higher mean F1'.

Section 4.3 (p.5) states the Tables 1-2 implementation materializes a full private copy per query. Does anything in Tables 1-2 then depend on the fork/COW/rebinding design at all, and if not, why is that design in the abstract and Figure 1 as part of the measured protocol rather than as future work?

Table 18 (p.27) shows the paged-prefix baseline and the audited hybrid fork with identical final (2.229 GiB) and peak (2.843 GiB) values, and the fork 1.93 GiB worse on generation increment. Given this, what is the deployment argument for the borrowed-GDN fork over paged-prefix block sharing, other than auditability?

XQuant (Tomar et al., 2025) caches quantized layer-input activations and rematerializes K/V, i.e. it is a compute-for-memory trade on a non-KV intermediate object with a reported ~7.7x saving at <0.1 ppl degradation. That is the same thesis as Q-CoMem's Write/Read. Why is it given one clause in Section 2 and omitted from both Table 14 and Table 19? What is the technical distinction beyond 'hybrid rather than dense'?

Appendix Table 16 (p.26) reports that all split rows hold only 71.89% top-1 agreement with vanilla dense on the MLX control, while the main text frames quality as -0.45 F1. How should a reader reconcile a 28-point top-1 divergence with 'bounded measured quality', and does the Qasper/2WikiMQA F1 metric simply absorb divergence that a stricter metric would expose?

Concurrent work on replay-based hybrid prefix caching has appeared (e.g. Tail-Replay, arXiv 2608.30310, 31 Aug 2026; LinearKV, arXiv 2608.11231). These are too recent to be a citation obligation, but they attack the same recurrent-state-reuse problem by replaying rather than storing. Would you position Q-CoMem against them in a revision, particularly on whether quantized state storage beats short-tail replay for the recurrent family?

The frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 point was selected among six on the same 60-item panel (Section 5.4, p.7). Is any held-out estimate of its quality delta available, or does the -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] interval remain the only estimate for a selected arm?

issues.location: Abstract p.1; Figure 1 and caption p.3; Section 4.3 p.5; Section 4.4 p.5; Section 5.1 'Executed systems' p.6; Section 5.5 p.8; Section 5.6 p.9
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract states 'online Read dequantizes and forks that state, keeps mutable request state private, and replays the query before reconstructing the suffix,' and Figure 1 draws Write/Retain/Read/Audit as one protocol. But Section 4.3 (p.5) states that 'the Transformers implementation behind Tables 1 and 2 instead materializes a full private copy of the dequantized entry per query, so it shares nothing and exercises neither borrowing nor copy-on-write.' Section 4.4 and Section 5.1 state that every FORKAUDIT verdict and every allocator number come from a different system (vLLM 0.26 + Transformers, full-prefix BF16 KV, no split depth, no quantization, PG-19). Section 5.6 concedes 'ownership there transfers by design argument only.' No table in the paper reports a single execution in which a packed split entry is shared across concurrent requests under the described ownership discipline.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's identity is the composition of two parts -- a quantized whole-entry split-replay store, and an audited immutable/mutable ownership boundary for sharing it. Each part is measured only in a configuration from which the other is absent. The composite therefore has zero end-to-end evidence, and the two most likely places for the composition to fail (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime -- named by the authors themselves on p.5 as 'untested') are exactly the ones nobody exercised. For a novelty/positioning assessment this is decisive: the delta over CoMem-plus-standard-quantization is claimed to be the ownership-safe hybrid fork, and that delta is not demonstrated on the system it is claimed for. Repeated disclosure does not convert an unevaluated design into a contribution.
issues.required_fix: Either (a) run FORKAUDIT's ownership targets on the actual quantized split-replay Read path at j=7 with Q4/Q4/Q8 and shared document tensors, and report Store, F1 and allocator endpoints from that single composed system; or (b) restructure the paper so that the abstract, Figure 1 and the contribution list describe two separately evaluated artifacts and stop presenting a composite protocol. If (b), the fork/COW/rebinding description must move out of Section 4.3's description of the Read path that Tables 1-2 measure.
issues.verification_test: A single table in which one execution reports, for the same run identifier: packed Q4/Q4/Q8 entry at j=7, N>1 resident requests sharing the dequantized document view, per-target FORKAUDIT coverage and verdicts, retained Store, mean F1 against a full-prefix arm from that same execution, and allocator final/peak. If the paper cannot produce such a row, the composite claim is not supported.
issues.evidence_needed: One end-to-end run identifier and archive binding the quantized Read path to the seven ownership targets, with the three currently untested packed-entry obligations (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime) covered.

issues.location: Abstract p.1; Section 5.2 p.7; Table 1 operating-point block p.7; Section 5.4 p.8; Table 19 KVTuner row p.28; Section 2 'KV and state quantization' p.3
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract's competitive claim is that against 'the quantized exact-cache arm: full-prefix Q8 retains 56.438 MiB/document at -3.78 points [-9.12, 0.32], so the frozen policy is 5.84x smaller than that arm with a 3.41-point higher mean F1.' That arm is the paper's own uniform Q8 application of its own codec. An 8-bit group-64 asymmetric quantizer losing 3.78 LongBench F1 points is out of line with every KV-quantization result the paper cites: KIVI (2-bit, tuning-free), KVQuant, and the paper's own Table 19 (p.28) which records KVTuner as 'nearly lossless 3.25-bit mixed-precision KV.' None of KIVI, KVQuant, KVTuner, AsymKV or XQuant is implemented as a comparator anywhere in the paper; Table 19 is explicitly 'literature context, not ForkAudit evidence' and carries no matched numbers.
issues.why_it_matters: The strongest positive comparative statement in the paper is against a straw quantized cache, and it is phrased in the abstract as if it placed Q-CoMem above the KV-quantization family it cites. Either the arm is defective, in which case the 3.41-point claim evaporates, or 8-bit quantization really does cost 3.78 F1 on this stack, in which case the paper has found something surprising about GDN state under affine quantization that contradicts the cited literature and must be reported and diagnosed as such rather than used as a foil. Both readings undercut the claim as written, and the second would be more interesting than the claim it currently supports.
issues.required_fix: Diagnose the full-prefix Q8 arm: report per-state-family ablation (attention KV only at Q8, GDN recurrent only at Q8) so the source of the 3.78-point loss is attributed. Then either fix the arm and re-report, or keep it and add at least one published layer-wise mixed-precision KV baseline (KVTuner or AsymKV) at matched retained bytes on the same 60 items. Restate the abstract sentence to name the arm as 'a uniform-Q8 application of our own codec' and drop the unqualified '3.41-point higher mean F1' unless a paired interval between the two arms supports it.
issues.verification_test: Add rows for full-prefix Q8-attention-only and full-prefix Q8-GDN-only on the 60-item operating-point run, plus one cited-method baseline at ~56 MiB/document. If the attribution shows the loss is concentrated in one family, the comparison must be re-scoped; if a cited method reaches ~56 MiB/document at under 1 F1 point of loss, the abstract claim must be withdrawn.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-family Q8 ablation on the 60-item cohort and at least one reimplemented or ported KV-quantization baseline at matched bytes.

issues.location: Abstract p.1; Contribution bullet 3 p.2; Section 5.5 'Allocator endpoints' p.8; Table 18 p.27
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract leads the ownership result with '4.901 to 2.229 GiB final (54.5%) and 4.920 to 2.843 GiB peak (42.2%) at N = 32', against a full-copy arm. Table 18 (p.27) shows the paged-prefix baseline -- shared-doc KV / materialized GDN base, i.e. PagedAttention block sharing from 2023 -- achieving exactly 2.229 and 2.843 GiB, identical to the audited hybrid fork, while the audited fork is 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB on generation increment, i.e. roughly 1.93 GiB worse. The paper discloses this ('our audited fork ties on both endpoints ... buying auditable request-local state, not fewer allocator bytes').
issues.why_it_matters: As measured, the ownership component of Q-CoMem delivers no allocator benefit over prior art and is materially worse on one endpoint. Placing the 54.5%/42.2% figures in the abstract's headline position, with the tie relegated to a subordinate clause, inflates the contribution relative to what the paper's own table shows. A reader skimming the abstract will take away a memory saving that the paper does not claim on inspection. The correct novelty framing -- 'ties existing block sharing on bytes, adds auditability, costs 1.93 GiB at generation' -- is a much weaker but honest claim.
issues.required_fix: Rewrite the abstract sentence so that the paged-prefix tie and the generation-increment regression are the primary statement and the full-copy control is secondary, e.g. 'our audited fork matches paged-prefix block sharing on final and peak allocator bytes at N=32 and is 1.93 GiB worse on generation increment, buying auditable request-local state rather than fewer bytes.' Apply the same reordering to contribution bullet 3 (p.2).
issues.verification_test: Read the revised abstract in isolation and check that a reader cannot come away believing the ownership design reduces memory relative to any deployed prior-art baseline. Confirm the 54.5%/42.2% figures never appear without the paged-prefix tie in the same sentence.
issues.evidence_needed: None; this is a framing fix against the paper's existing Table 18.

issues.location: Section 2 'KV and state quantization' p.3; Table 14 p.26; Table 19 pp.27-28
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's differentiating sentence is: 'each method compresses one homogeneous cache along a single execution path, whereas a hybrid split-replay entry is heterogeneous' (Section 2, p.3). XQuant (Tomar et al., 2025), which the paper cites, is precisely a method that does not compress a homogeneous KV cache along a single path: it quantizes and caches layer-input activations X and rematerializes K and V during decode, trading compute for memory, reporting up to ~7.7x memory savings at under 0.1 perplexity degradation (arXiv:2508.10395). It is disposed of in a single subordinate clause -- 'KIVI, KVQuant, and XQuant fix the grouping axis or the tensor quantized' -- and appears in neither the positioning table (Table 14, p.26) nor the published-context table (Table 19, pp.27-28), which do include PagedAttention, Prompt Cache, SGLang, ChunkAttention, Hydragen, Palu, Preble, Marconi, KVTuner and HYPIC.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central mechanism -- persist a quantized intermediate representation and pay recomputation to avoid retaining downstream state -- is XQuant's thesis, applied at a different cut point and on a hybrid backbone. Under a novelty lens, the closest prior art on the paper's own core idea is the one entry given the least engagement, and the sentence that establishes the paper's differentiation is stated in a way that XQuant already falsifies for the dense case. Credit assignment here is not accurate, and a reader cannot judge whether the hybrid extension is the substantive step it is claimed to be.
issues.required_fix: Give XQuant a dedicated paragraph in Section 2 and a row in Table 14 and Table 19, stating its mechanism (quantized activation caching plus K/V rematerialization), its reported compression and quality, and the precise technical distinction from Q-CoMem (single-layer input activations recomputed within a layer vs a depth-j boundary residual plus lower-layer hybrid state replayed through [0,j); dense vs hybrid; no ownership/mutability question in XQuant). Revise the 'single execution path / homogeneous cache' sentence so it is true of the works it covers.
issues.verification_test: Check that Section 2 states, in one sentence, what Q-CoMem retains that XQuant does not and why the hybrid recurrent family makes the difference non-trivial; and that Table 19 reports XQuant's native compression/quality alongside KVTuner's.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiments; a positioning paragraph and two table rows. Optionally, a bounded same-checkpoint XQuant transfer analogous to the existing Hydragen/Palu ports in Table 20 (p.28) would settle it directly.

issues.location: Abstract p.1; contribution bullets pp.2-3; Section 2 pp.2-3; Table 14 p.26; Appendix C p.17; Section 5.5 p.8
issues.observed_evidence: Each named component is disclaimed by the authors: the split-replay primitive is prior CoMem (Section 2 p.2-3; Table 14 p.26); the quantizer is 'the standard asymmetric affine quantizer ... the form FlexGen already used' (p.3); per-layer widths are 'an application of an established design surface, not a new selection method' (p.3); FORKAUDIT's alias finding is caught equally by 'a persistent-base content invariant' so 'the increment is transition-time localization, not exclusive detection' (Section 5.5 p.8; Table 17 p.26 shows base-invariant fail 8/8 on the pre-fix lanes). What remains is the whole-entry denominator and the resulting measurement. Appendix C (p.17) shows every quantized row satisfies the format identity exactly (180/180) and that the like-for-like quantization step is 2.969x against a 3.5556x Q4 ceiling -- i.e. no reported compression exceeds what the chosen bit widths arithmetically imply.
issues.why_it_matters: A novelty assessment has to ask what a reader learns that they could not have computed. Given a bit vector and a component inventory, every Store number in the paper follows from Eq. 3; the only genuinely empirical outputs are the F1 deltas and the timing. The residual scientific claim is therefore 'quantizing a hybrid split-replay entry to Q4/Q4/Q8 costs about 0.45 F1 on 60 Qasper/2WikiMQA items and roughly 0.5 s of TTFT.' That is a legitimate but narrow measurement, and the paper's framing (a named system, a named audit protocol, three contribution bullets) presents it as more. The honesty is real and creditable; the contribution boundary is nonetheless thin for ICLR.
issues.required_fix: State plainly in the introduction what the residual claim is after the disclaimers -- one sentence naming the empirical quantity that could not have been predicted from the format arithmetic -- and drop or demote framing that implies a new mechanism. Then strengthen the residual claim: sweep j (currently validated against exactly one alternative, j=13, Section 5.6 p.9), add a second model family beyond Qwen3.5 for the quality panel, or add a second task family beyond Qasper/2WikiMQA, so the measured quality cost has some generality.
issues.verification_test: Ask whether any headline number in the paper would change if a reader recomputed it from Eq. 3 and Table 4 without running anything. Everything that survives that test is the contribution; the introduction should claim exactly that set.
issues.evidence_needed: A j sweep on the 60-item cohort and at least one additional model or task family for the Store-F1 panel.

issues.observed_evidence: The abstract asserts '5.84x smaller than that arm with a 3.41-point higher mean F1' as a flat statement. Section 5.4 (p.8) discloses that 'we computed no paired interval between those two arms and their intervals against the shared reference overlap, so the retained-state ordering is the firmer of the two.' Table 1 shows full-prefix Q8 at -3.78 [-9.12, 0.32] -- an interval that crosses zero -- and the frozen point at -0.37 [-1.97, 1.08], also crossing zero. The 3.41-point figure is thus a difference of two point estimates neither of which is separated from the shared reference.
issues.why_it_matters: The body applies the correct standard and the abstract does not. Readers and downstream citers take the abstract number. Given that the paper elsewhere is scrupulous about not asserting equivalence from an interval that crosses zero, the asymmetry is conspicuous.
issues.required_fix: In the abstract, either report a paired bootstrap interval for the frozen-point-vs-Q8 contrast (both arms exist in the same execution, so the paired resample is available at no experimental cost) or attach the same qualifier the body uses: 'a 3.41-point higher mean F1, for which we compute no paired interval.'
issues.verification_test: Compute the paired 10,000-resample interval on the 60 common items for frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 minus full-prefix Q8 in the operating-point run and report it in Table 1 and the abstract. If it crosses zero, the abstract must say so.
issues.evidence_needed: One additional paired bootstrap interval from already-archived per-item F1 values.

issues.location: Abstract p.1; Section 5.2 p.6-7; Table 2 'Reduction' column p.8; Conclusion p.9
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract, Section 5.2, Table 2 and the conclusion all lead with the native-dtype ratios (14.10x; 88.68-94.01% reduction), and only afterwards note that 30.000 of 136.235 MiB is FP32 GDN excess and the like-for-like figure is 10.9965x with a 2.969x packing step (Appendix C, p.17). Table 2 (p.8) reports its Reduction column only in native-dtype terms; the all-BF16 restatement appears only in a footnote and in Appendix C.
issues.why_it_matters: Roughly a quarter of the headline compression comes from the unmodified stack storing GDN recurrent state in FP32, which any deployment could fix by casting to BF16 without adopting Q-CoMem at all. Leading with the inflated ratio in four separate places while the corrected ratio appears once, in an appendix, is a consistent directional bias in presentation even though nothing is concealed.
issues.required_fix: Print both ratios side by side wherever a compression factor appears: abstract, Section 5.2, Table 1's compression column, Table 2's Reduction column, and the conclusion. Add an all-BF16 Reduction column to Table 2.
issues.verification_test: Grep the manuscript for every occurrence of a compression ratio or percentage reduction and confirm each is accompanied by its all-BF16 counterpart within the same sentence or table row.
issues.evidence_needed: None; restatement of existing Appendix C numbers.

issues.location: Abstract p.1; Tables 1 (p.7) and 2 (p.8); Appendices D-J pp.18-36; Figure 3 caption p.18
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract is a single ~45-line block containing at least fourteen distinct numeric claims, each with its own scope qualifier, with no paragraph structure separating capacity, quality, latency and ownership. Two different full-prefix references (136.235 and 140.34 MiB/doc) and a third (106.235) appear across Tables 1, 2 and 4, reconciled only in a dense footnote. The appendices contain 30 tables, the majority of which (Tables 5-13, 24-30) document internal audit bookkeeping -- receipt counts, file trees, bytecode file counts, replay wall times -- with no stated mapping to a manuscript claim other than the Table 30 artifact map. Figure 3 (p.18) is captioned by the authors as 'not experimental evidence.'
issues.why_it_matters: The paper is precise but the reader has to reconstruct the claim structure themselves. For a reviewer, the density is the main obstacle to verifying which of three cohorts supports which number, and the appendix volume dilutes the material that actually bears on the contribution.
issues.required_fix: Restructure the abstract into four short claim blocks (capacity, quality, latency, ownership) with one scope qualifier each. Adopt a single canonical full-prefix reference for the main text and relegate the cohort-difference reconciliation to Appendix C. Move audit bookkeeping tables (receipt counts, file/bytecode counts, replay times) to the artifact package and keep only tables a claim depends on in the appendix. Replace or drop Figure 3, which the caption itself says carries no evidence.
issues.verification_test: A reader given only pages 1-9 should be able to state the paper's four claims and their cohorts without consulting an appendix. Count appendix tables that no main-text sentence cites; each such table is a candidate for removal.

issues.location: Appendix H, Table 16 p.26; Section 5.4 p.7; Abstract p.1
issues.observed_evidence: Table 16 (p.26) reports that on the Apple M4 Pro MLX control, all Q-CoMem split rows (BF16, Q8, Q4 alike) hold only 71.89% top-1 agreement with vanilla dense, while retaining 100% agreement with each other. The main text's quality claim is a -0.45 F1 mean difference on LongBench Qasper/2WikiMQA. The paper labels Table 16 'motivation only' and says it shows 'why split-family agreement does not replace a dense or independently implemented oracle,' but never reconciles the 28-point top-1 divergence with the -0.45 F1 framing.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's own strongest signal that split replay changes model behaviour appears in an appendix labelled motivation, while the abstract's quality statement rests on a metric (LongBench F1, greedy, at most 32 tokens) that can absorb substantial token-level divergence. A reader deciding whether 'bounded measured quality' is trustworthy needs the two placed together.
issues.required_fix: Report token-level agreement with the full-prefix arm on the 60-item H20 cohort alongside the F1 deltas (Appendix B already establishes 58/60 identical greedy sequences for split Q16 -- extend this to the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 point and report it in Table 1). In the limitations section, state explicitly that F1 on these two tasks is the only quality metric and that the Mac control shows the split family can diverge from dense at the token level.
issues.verification_test: Add an 'identical greedy sequences vs full-prefix (out of 60)' column to Table 1. If the frozen point's value is materially below 58/60, the 'bounded quality' framing needs revisiting.
issues.evidence_needed: Token-sequence agreement counts from the already-archived 60-item predictions.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concern warranting a flag. The paper uses public PG-19, Qasper and 2WikiMQA data, involves no human subjects, and includes an ethics statement (p.9) that correctly notes it makes no safety, bias or privacy assessment and that efficiency gains can increase deployment scale. The LLM-use disclosure (p.9) is unusually complete, stating that LLM assistance covered drafting, related-work triage, internal critiques and experiment specifications, with authors adjudicating and taking responsibility. Under the novelty lens I note only that the CoMem citations (Liu et al., 2026a;b) are, on the public record, by the same first author as this submission's likely author group; third-person self-citation is standard and compliant with double-blind, but the extent of overlap with the authors' own prior system is material to the novelty judgement and is handled honestly in Section 2 and Table 14. One citation-hygiene oddity: the CoMem author list as printed includes the entries 'Key, Rayying' (2026a) and 'Rayying, Key' (2026b), which appear to be handles rather than names and are inconsistently ordered between the two entries.

The reviewer read the full 36-page PDF via pdftotext -layout and inspected pages 3, 4 and 18 as rendered images. WebSearch and WebFetch were used solely to verify external positioning claims: XQuant (arXiv:2508.10395), Marconi (MLSys 2025), HYPIC (arXiv:2607.01299), the cited CoMem preprint (arXiv:2607.28263), and a check for concurrent replay-based hybrid caching work (arXiv:2608.30310, arXiv:2608.11231). No repository, LaTeX source, sibling directory, evidence file, author note or prior review was consulted. All scores and issue severities are the reviewer's own judgement against the supplied rubric.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A single execution in which the packed Q4/Q4/Q8 split entry at j=7 is shared across N>1 resident requests under the Section 4.3 ownership discipline, with FORKAUDIT coverage/verdicts, Store, F1 and allocator endpoints all reported from that one run. This alone would move the composite claim from design argument to evidence and would lift the score by at least one step.

A diagnosis of the full-prefix Q8 arm's 3.78-point loss with per-state-family attribution, plus one cited layer-wise mixed-precision KV baseline (KVTuner or AsymKV) at matched retained bytes on the same 60 items. If the frozen policy still wins on both bytes and F1 against a competently implemented baseline, the comparative claim becomes real.

A dedicated positioning treatment of XQuant with either a bounded same-checkpoint transfer (in the style of the existing Hydragen/Palu ports, Table 20) or an argued technical distinction that survives the fact that XQuant also stores a quantized intermediate and recomputes.

Generality evidence for the quality cost: a j sweep beyond the single j=13 control, and the Store-F1 panel on a second hybrid model family or a second task family, showing the -0.45 F1 point estimate is not specific to Qwen3.5 on two LongBench tasks.
A paired bootstrap interval between the frozen point and full-prefix Q8 that excludes zero, computed from the already-archived per-item values.

Any regime in which the capacity win converts into a measured deployment benefit -- more documents admitted, higher concurrency, or lower peak VRAM -- rather than retained tensor payload alone. The paper currently and correctly declines to claim this; demonstrating it would change the significance assessment materially.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Evidence that the full-prefix Q8 comparator's 3.78-point loss is an implementation defect, which would remove the paper's only favourable comparative claim and leave a system that is worse than exact caching on TTFT, throughput and F1, and better only on a byte count partly explained by dtype narrowing.

Evidence that the CoMem prior work (Liu et al., 2026a;b) already reports whole-entry or hybrid-state retained-payload accounting, which would eliminate contribution bullet 1 as well as the split-replay primitive.

A demonstration that the described fork/COW/rebinding discipline does not compose with the packed Read path -- e.g. that dequantized-view immutability or residual-chunk binding fails at j=7 under Q4 -- which would falsify the composite protocol rather than merely leave it unevaluated.

Evidence that casting the stack's FP32 GDN recurrent state to BF16 and applying an existing off-the-shelf KV quantizer to the full prefix reaches comparable retained bytes at lower quality and latency cost than the split path, which would remove the operating point's reason to exist.

Discovery that any number in Tables 1 or 2 was pooled across the three non-pooled cohorts, or that a blank Recall cell was ever treated as a measurement, which would undercut the paper's central evidentiary discipline.
review_limitations: PDF-only access. I could not inspect the referenced artifact packages, the FORKAUDIT implementation, the quantizer source, or the archived per-item F1 values, so every replay count, hash binding and coverage verdict in Appendices A, E, F and J is taken as asserted and not verified.

The suspicion that the full-prefix Q8 arm is defective is an inference from the cited literature and from the paper's own Table 19, not from inspecting that arm's code or outputs. The authors may have a correct explanation.

CoMem (Liu et al., 2026a;b) postdates my training data; I verified its existence, title, authors and mechanism via the arXiv abstract only, and could not read it in full. My judgement of the Q-CoMem-over-CoMem delta therefore rests on this paper's own characterisation plus that abstract.

Tail-Replay (arXiv:2608.30310, 31 Aug 2026) and LinearKV (arXiv:2608.11231) appeared within days of this manuscript's compilation date and are treated as concurrent; I raise them as a question, not as a citation obligation, and they do not affect the score.
I did not attempt to verify the LongBench F1 computation, the bootstrap implementation, or any timing measurement.
My lens is novelty and positioning. Soundness and presentation scores reflect what was visible from that vantage point and should be weighted against reviewers assigned those dimensions.
